key_insight: Well-tuned sinusoidal pitching boosts turbine power, but net flow-to-pitch energy transfer alone does not guarantee improved performance.
engineering_relevance: Joint power and pitching-energy maps identify promising motions for passive or assisted blade-pitch designs with a margin against assumed dissipation.
method: Tested 480 prescribed-pitch conditions on a single blade moving along a circular path in a water channel.
Varied pitch amplitude and phase at four tip-speed ratios from 1.25 to 3.14.
Combined pitching-energy maps and virtual damping with phase-resolved force measurements and particle image velocimetry.
evidence_signal: At tip-speed ratios of 1.25 and 3.14, the best-tested pitching motions raised cycle-averaged power coefficients from 0.0047 to 0.1037 and from 0.4698 to 0.5948, respectively.
watch_item: Prescribed-pitch energy surpluses do not establish passive realizability; actual motion and performance depend on pitch dynamics and mechanical losses.
paper_title: Effects of sinusoidal pitch amplitude and phase on power extraction and pitching-energy exchange in a single-blade vertical-axis turbine model
